title: Metal Forward+: intermittent black squares from a single static OmniLight3D on Apple Silicon
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: Godot 4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f].
- Earlier Godot versions were not tested with this MRP.

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f] - macOS Sequoia 15.6.1 (24G90) - Metal 3.2 (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 Max (Apple7) - Apple M1 Max (10 threads)

### Issue description

Solid black, screen-aligned squares intermittently flash for a frame on lit 3D surfaces while the camera moves. They can appear on walls, the floor, or the ceiling. In the attached MRP they were easiest to see while walking backward, farther away from the positional light.

Expected behavior: lighting remains stable while the camera moves.

The MRP contains only generated box geometry, a basic camera controller, and one `OmniLight3D`. The light is completely static: shadows and flicker are disabled, and no light properties change after startup. There are no textures, custom shaders, post-processing effects, volumetric fog, or imported assets.

The same artifact originally appeared in a larger project. Disabling shadows, removing post-processing, and changing shadow-atlas settings did not eliminate it. Switching that project from Forward+ to Mobile eliminated the squares during extended playtesting.

This appears similar to the clustered positional-light artifacts discussed in:

- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/61108
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/45469
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104168

Those reports describe the same relevant pattern: OmniLight3D/SpotLight3D, screen-space squares, shadows not being required, and Mobile avoiding the problem. This may be a regression or a related issue in the native Metal Forward+ cluster-building path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached project on Apple Silicon macOS with Forward+.
2. Run the project. It uses a 320×240 internal viewport with integer scaling.
3. Move with WASD and look around with the mouse.
4. Face the lit surfaces and repeatedly walk toward and backward away from the light. The artifact is intermittent, so this may take a minute or two.
5. Observe a solid black square briefly replace part of a lit surface.

Shadows and light-energy flicker are both off initially. Press `1` to toggle shadows or `2` to toggle flicker.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[forward_plus_black_square_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29910331/forward_plus_black_square_mrp.zip)
